title: Distinct result verdicts
summary: Failed, skipped, unavailable, denied, and invalid-audit outcomes must remain distinguishable.

sections.label: Recommended practice
sections.text: Keep success, failure, partial verification, unavailable environments, denied access, invalid audits, and unrun checks distinct. Choose labels that fit your project and define the evidence required for each outcome.

sections.label: Example source: Talos verdict template
sections.text: The inspected Talos summary template provides the following verdict vocabulary. The explanations show a proposed use for your project, not a mandatory standard or observed test results.

sections.label: Example verdict vocabulary
rows: Required applicable evidence supports the outcome
Observed behavior violates the expected invariant
Only part of the intended scope was verified
The operation/environment cannot support the check
The fixture or audit design is invalid

sections.label: Project example
sections.text: Missing Neptune access is not a failed query. A skipped integration test is not a pass. A broken fixture is not necessarily an implementation defect.

confidence: High for inspected vocabulary. Moderate for project adaptation

catalog.applicability: Use this when defining the outcome labels for checks in your project, so that skipped, unavailable, denied, invalid audit and unrun outcomes stay distinct from pass and fail. The Talos vocabulary is an example to adapt, not a mandatory standard.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
